'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**[[Mekelle offensive (2020)|Mekelle offensive]]
***[[Ethiopian National Defense Force|Federal forces]] say that they have seized the town of [[Wukro]] in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Tigray Region]] as they advance on the [[regions of Ethiopia|region]]'s capital [[Mekelle]]. [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] (TPLF) leader [[Debretsion Gebremichael]] confirms that [[government of Ethiopia|government]] forces had started an operation to capture Mekelle, saying his forces are "ready to die in defence of our right to administer our region". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-55111061 (BBC News)]
***[[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] says that the Ethiopian military is in "full control" of Mekelle after entering the regional capital with limited resistance and are now searching for Tigrayan officials. [[Chief of General Staff (Ethiopia)|Chief of General Staff]] [[Birhanu Jula Gelalcha]] says government forces have now "completely controlled Mekelle", and that 7,000  Northern Command members being held hostage by the TPLF have been freed. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/11/28/ethiopian-army-takes-full-control-of-tigray-capital-abiy-says (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[United States|U.S.]] [[Embassy]] in [[Asmara]] reports several explosions in the [[Eritrea]]n capital. The TPLF has previously [[Asmara rocket attacks|fired rockets at the capital]] during the conflict. [https://apnews.com/article/eritrea-abiy-ahmed-ethiopia-asmara-kenya-52bb678b19f48e036470caae4aabdb6a (AP)]
*[[Assassination of Iranian nuclear scientists]]
**[[Mohsen_Fakhrizadeh#Assassination|Assassination of Mohsen Fakhrizadeh]]
***[[President of Iran|Iranian president]] [[Hassan Rouhani]] vows to "respond" to [[Israel]], whom the regime has accused of orchestrating the killing, "at the proper time." [https://www.cnbc.com/2020/11/28/irans-president-hassan-rouhani-accuses-israel-for-the-killing-of-nuclear-scientist.html (CNBC)]
***The [[supercarrier]] [[USS Nimitz|USS ''Nimitz'']] is deployed to the [[Persian Gulf]] from its station in [[Bahrain]]. The [[U.S. Navy]] maintains that the ship's deployment was not related to "any specific threat." [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-iran-nuclear-scientist-usa-navy-idUKKBN2880DJ (Reuters)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Koshebe massacre]]
***[[Boko Haram]] [[jihadist]]s attack a [[agriculture in Nigeria|farm]] in [[Jere, Borno|Jere]], [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]], killing at least 43 people. The [[massacre]] reportedly occurred during the morning, when most workers were harvesting rice. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-nigeria-security/militant-attack-on-farm-in-northern-nigeria-leaves-40-dead-sources-idUKKBN2880MA?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[College of Cardinals]]
**[[Wilton Daniel Gregory]], [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Washington|Archbishop of Washington]], becomes the first [[African Americans|African American]] to earn the rank of [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinal]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/pope-francis-wilton-gregory-new-cardinal/2020/11/27/d07ad7f6-2e66-11eb-9dd6-2d0179981719_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A major [[search and rescue]] operation is underway following a [[mining accident|collapse]] at a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] in [[Bindura]], [[Zimbabwe]]. Around 30 miners remain unaccounted for since the collapse, while six men have emerged alive from the mine. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2020/nov/28/dozens-feared-dead-in-zimbabwe-mine-collapse-as-rescue-efforts-continue (''The Guardian'')]
*The city of [[Nuoro]], on the island of [[Sardinia]], [[Italy]], is affected by [[floods|flooding]] and subsequent [[mudflows]] caused by heavy rains, killing at least three people. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-55115241 (BBC News)]

*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]

[https://montreal.ctvnews.ca/quebec-breaks-record-for-new-covid-19-cases-as-number-of-deaths-surpass-7-000-1.5208593 (CFCF-DT)]

****The number of cases in [[Canada]] exceeds 360,000. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7490677/coronavirus-canada-update-nov-28/ (Global News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] reports 12,081 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the pandemic began. [https://www.theyucatantimes.com/2020/11/new-record-of-covid-19-cases-for-mexico-in-one-day/ (''The Yucatan Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****Hairdressers and other non-essential shops in [[France]] reopen for the first time since October after the country eases its second nationwide [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/nov/28/shops-reopen-in-france-as-national-lockdown-eases (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] reports a record 121 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,223. [https://www.ekathimerini.com/259707/article/ekathimerini/news/record-121-deaths-from-the-coronavirus (''Ekathimerini'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] surpasses 200,000 total cases of COVID-19. In addition, a record of 152 new deaths in the last 24 hours is also reported. [https://hungarytoday.hu/coronavirus-saturday-covid-hungary-record-death-fatalities-new-cases/ (Hungary Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 182 new deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 13,373. The country also reports 30,103 new cases, including asymptomatic cases, a new record since the pandemic after asymptomatic cases are included. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/turkey-s-daily-coronavirus-death-toll-hits-record-for-sixth-day-in-a-row/46191054 (Swiss Info)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] surpasses 700,000 total cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] after a record 16,294 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-16294-new-cases-184-new-deaths-362473-active-cases.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Belarus]]
****[[Belarus]] reports 1,691 cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record, bringing the total number of cases to 133,324. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-11/28/c_139549768.htm (Xinhua News Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] announces that [[Nadhim Zahawi]] will be appointed as the country's vaccine rollout minister. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-55115037 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] reports 2,684 new cases in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record since the beginning of the outbreak. [https://www.nippon.com/en/news/yjj2020112800321/japan-confirms-record-2-684-new-coronavirus-cases.html (Nippon.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Myanmar]]
****[[Myanmar]] extends their restrictions for another 15 days until December 15, according to an announcement made by de facto leader [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in the country. The current restrictions are due to end on November 30. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-11-28/myanmar-extends-covid-19-restrictions-for-2-weeks-until-dec-15 (Bloomberg)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***The first batch of one million doses of [[Sinopharm]]'s vaccine arrives in [[Casablanca]], [[Morocco]]. Morocco has ordered an initial 10 million doses. [https://northafricapost.com/45627-a-chinese-delegation-visits-casablanca-to-discuss-sinopharm-vaccine-manufacturing-in-morocco.html (North Africa Post)]
***The first doses of [[Pfizer]]'s potential vaccine are flown to the [[United States]] from [[Belgium]]. [https://thehill.com/policy/transportation/aviation/527835-first-doses-of-pfizer-vaccine-being-flown-to-us-from-belgium (''The Hill'')] 
*[[Avian influenza]]
**[[2020 H5N8 outbreak]]
***[[South Korea]]'s [[Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (South Korea)|Agriculture Ministry]] reports the first case of highly pathogenic [[Influenza A virus subtype H5N8|H5N8]] [[avian influenza]] among domestic [[poultry]] at a duck [[agriculture in South Korea|farm]] in the city of [[Jeongeup]], [[North Jeolla Province]]. [https://m.koreatimes.co.kr/pages/article.asp?newsIdx=300065 (''The Korea Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Egypt–South Sudan relations]]
**[[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] visits [[South Sudan]], making him the first [[President of Egypt]] to do so. [https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/Egypt-leader-in-1st-South-Sudan-visit-talks-Nile-15759901.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
*[[European migrant crisis]], [[France–United Kingdom relations]]
**[[United Kingdom|UK]] [[Home Secretary]] [[Priti Patel]] and [[France|French]] [[Minister of the Interior (France)|Minister of the Interior]] [[Gérald Darmanin]] announce an agreement to curb [[illegal immigration|illegal migrant crossings]] in the [[English Channel]]. As part of the measures, costing the UK an additional 31.4 million euro, French border patrol officers will double their patrols on French beaches beginning next week, while enhancing surveillance, including increasing the use of drones to detect migrant boats. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-55116475 (BBC News)] [https://www.lavoixdunord.fr/900488/article/2020-11-29/traversees-de-la-manche-plus-de-patrouilles-et-de-drones-pour-freiner-les (''La Voix du Nord'')]
*[[Montenegro–Serbia relations]]
**[[Montenegro]] and [[Serbia]] expel their respective ambassadors following controversial comments by Serbian ambassador Vladimir Bozovic, who described the [[Kingdom of Montenegro]]'s decision to merge with the [[Kingdom of Yugoslavia]] in [[1918]] as a "liberation". He was accused of "interfering in Montenegro's internal affairs" and was given 72 hours to leave the country by the Montenegrin government. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-55118403 (BBC News)]
